items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Terminology 47:1
items.html: When the illumination of the coupling that is made at the time of the refining of the screen descends from the upper phase to the lower phase that is empty of her light — as, for example, when the screen was refined from phase three to phase two and phase three was emptied of her light — then the illumination of the coupling descends from phase two into the empty phase three. And since the record that remains in phase three is opposite to the descending illumination, they therefore strike and clash one against the other. Indeed, the descending reflected light prevails over the record, whose coupling has already ceased, and the reflected light descends into the vessel, and the record, which cannot be together with it in one subject, departs from there. And this illumination of the coupling that descends into the empty vessel is called “the falling sparks.” The reason is that very soon the coupling ceases from phase two as well and rises to phase one, as is known, and the illuminations are found to be extinguished, and the record returns and descends to its vessel. For now the descending reflected light has no rank whatsoever over the record, since both of them are found after the departure of their coupling; and since the light of the record is incomparably greater than the descending reflected light, the record therefore now prevails over them and nullifies the illumination of the sparks that fall to its vessel, so that it can clothe there. And this matter is called striking and clashing, for at one time the descending reflected light prevails and at another time the record prevails, as explained. (Part 4, Chapter 3, Item 11)
